mainTopic: The end of the קנין פירות discussion, the close of פרק השולח, and the opening משנה and גמרא of פרק הניזקין on which grade of land pays each kind of claim.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument over whether owning a field's produce counts as owning the field itself. The גמרא brings support for ריש לקיש, who says it does not: a פסוק about selling 'years of crops,' and a ברייתא about a בכור. אביי adds that a husband needs הרשאה from his wife to go to court over her land, unless the case also involves the produce, because of a מיגו. The chapter השולח then ends, and the new chapter הניזקין begins. Its משנה ranks land for payment: נזיקין from עידית, a debt from בינונית, and a כתובה from זיבורית. It then lists limits on collecting, ending with rules made מפני תיקון העולם. The גמרא asks how the נזיקין rule can be a rabbinic fix when a פסוק teaches it. אביי answers that this fits רבי ישמעאל's view, which leads to a debate over that view that continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: The verse behind ריש לקיש's view
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's source: the Torah describes selling a field as selling a number of years of crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: "According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק that ריש לקיש uses to prove his view. The Torah says a field is sold for a number of years of crops, not as the field itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a field is sold before the יובל, the פסוק says what is really sold is 'years of crops.' So the buyer only owns the produce, and the field itself still belongs to the seller. This shows that owning the produce is not the same as owning the land.

keyTerms.meaning: crops, yields of produce
he shall sell
ownership of the produce only
ownership of the item itself

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the end of ריש לקיש's proof from just before this section, quoting the exact words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: "According to the number of years of crops
he shall sell to you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's scriptural source from the preceding discussion.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:15, where a sale of land is described as a sale of years of crops.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a בכור supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A בכור takes a double portion in a field his father sold, which returns in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא that supports this, as it is taught: A firstborn takes a double portion in a field that returns to his father in the יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports ריש לקיש. It says a בכור gets a double share even of a field his father had sold, which comes back in the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור only gets a double portion of what his father actually owned when he died. If the buyer's ownership of the produce counted as owning the field, the father would not have owned it at his death. Since the בכור does get a double share, the field must still count as the father's, just as ריש לקיש says.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה
firstborn son
a double portion
the Jubilee year, when sold fields return to their original owners

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear halachic case where ownership of the land itself stays with the seller even while someone else eats the produce.

phrases.english: There is a ברייתא that supports this, as it is taught:
A firstborn takes a double portion
in a field that returns to his father in the יובל.
phrases.notes: This means a field the father sold, which was going to come back in the יובל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא in support of ריש לקיש after his scriptural source.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that a בכור takes a double portion in a sold field that returns in the יובל, so the field still counts as owned by the father.

steps.title: אביי: a husband needs authorization for his wife's property
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition that a husband needs הרשאה from his wife to go to court over her property.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that a husband needs authorization regarding his wife's property.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shares a known rule. If there is a court case about land the wife brought into the marriage, the husband needs her written permission to argue it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband eats the produce of his wife's property (נכסי מלוג), but the land itself is hers. If owning the produce counted as owning the land, he would be the owner and would need no permission. Since he does need הרשאה, this fits ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: we hold, we have a tradition
his wife's property
authorization to act for someone in court

phrases.english: אביי said: We have a tradition:
A husband, regarding his wife's property,
needs authorization.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another rule that fits ריש לקיש's position.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's tradition that a husband, who owns only the produce, still needs הרשאה to go to court over the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband needs הרשאה from his wife to go to court over her property.

steps.title: When the husband does not need authorization
steps.stepSummary: אביי's rule applies only when the claim is not about the produce. If the produce is also involved, then by מיגו the husband can argue about the land too.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when the other side did not come to court about the produce. But if he came to court about the produce, then since the husband argues the case about the produce, he also argues the case about the land itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits אביי's rule. A husband needs הרשאה only when the case is about the land alone, not when the produce is also being claimed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The produce clearly belongs to the husband, so he can surely argue about it in court. The גמרא uses a מיגו: since he is already arguing about the produce, he can argue about the land too. So in that case no הרשאה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: went down (to court with a claim)
about the produce
since (one thing is true, the other follows as well)
argues the case, speaks in court
about the item itself (the land)

steps.whatToRemember: A husband needs his wife's הרשאה to go to court over her land, unless the case also involves the produce. Then, because of a מיגו, he can argue about the land as well.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the husband owns the land. He is simply allowed to argue about it in court because he is already there arguing about his produce.

phrases.english: And we said this only
when he did not come to court about the produce,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the other side in the case, the one making a claim against the husband.

phrases.english: but if he came to court about the produce,
since [the husband] argues the case about the produce,
he argues the case about the land itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of אביי's rule from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband needs הרשאה only when the claim does not involve the produce. If it does, he can argue about the land too because of a מיגו.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק השולח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally ends the chapter השולח with the traditional הדרן line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter השולח.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter השולח is finished here, and the גמרא marks its end with the הדרן formula. Nothing new is argued in this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the husband, the land, and the מיגו in the earlier steps is now closed. The line that follows starts a completely new chapter with a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the closing formula said when finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter now ending, taken from its first word

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One who sends"
phrases.notes: "One who sends" (הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ) is the chapter's name, taken from the first word of its opening משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that contained steps 1-4.

steps.title: Three grades of land for three kinds of payment
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens. The court pays נזיקין from the best land, a creditor from middle land, and a כתובה from the worst land. רבי מאיר says a כתובה is paid from middle land too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For injured people, the court assesses payment from the best-quality land. A creditor is paid from middle-quality land. A woman's כתובה is paid from the lowest-quality land. רבי מאיר says: a כתובה is also paid from middle-quality land.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה of the new chapter הניזקין starts by ranking three kinds of payment. Each kind is matched to a different quality of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each type of claim gets a different grade of land: נזיקין get עידית (best), a בעל חוב gets בינונית (middle), and a כתובה gets זיבורית (worst). The תנא קמא puts כתובה at the lowest level. רבי מאיר disagrees and raises כתובה up to the same level as a regular debt.

keyTerms.meaning: People who suffered damage and are owed payment
The best-quality land
Middle-quality land
The lowest-quality land
A creditor, someone owed a loan
The sum a husband commits to pay his wife if the marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: The grade of land is about which field the payer must hand over, not about how much is paid. The amount owed stays the same. Only the quality of the land used to pay it changes.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three grades (עידית, בינונית, זיבורית) are the base vocabulary for this whole chapter's discussion of collecting payment.

phrases.english: For injured parties, they assess payment from the best land,
and a creditor from middle-quality land,
and a woman's marriage contract from the lowest-quality land.
Rabbi Meir says:
A woman's marriage contract is also paid from middle-quality land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נזיקין are paid from עידית, a debt from בינונית, and a כתובה from זיבורית. רבי מאיר says a כתובה is paid from בינונית.

steps.title: No collecting from sold property while free property remains
steps.stepSummary: A creditor may not take liened land that was sold to others as long as the debtor still owns unsold land, even if that land is only זיבורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not collect from liened property that was sold while there is still free, unsold property, even if that free property is only the lowest-quality land.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit on where a creditor may collect from. He must first take from what the debtor still owns, before touching land that was sold to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a lien lets a creditor take land the debtor sold to a buyer. This rule says that power is only a last resort. As long as the debtor still owns any free land, even the worst kind, the buyers are left alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Collect payment
Liened property that the debtor has already sold to others
Free property the debtor still owns and has not sold

phrases.english: We do not collect from liened property
phrases.notes: This means land the debtor sold to a buyer after the debt began, so the creditor's lien still sits on it.

phrases.english: where there is free, unsold property,
even if that free property is the lowest-quality land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין נִפְרָעִין מִנְּכָסִים מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ נְכָסִים בְּנֵי חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by adding a limit to the collection rules of step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Free property, even זיבורית, must be used before sold, liened property.

steps.title: Collecting from orphans only from the worst land
steps.stepSummary: When a debtor has died and his יתומים inherited his land, a creditor may collect from them only זיבורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not collect from the property of orphans except from the lowest-quality land.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more limit: when the payer is יתומים who inherited the land, the creditor gets only the worst land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a creditor usually gets בינונית. Here that changes when the heirs are יתומים. Even a claim that would normally reach better land is lowered to זיבורית.

keyTerms.meaning: Property inherited by orphans from their father

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sets three grades of land (עידית for נזיקין, בינונית for a debt, זיבורית for a כתובה) and then adds two limits. Sold property is taken only when no free property is left, and יתומים pay only from זיבורית.

phrases.english: We do not collect from the property of orphans
except from the lowest-quality land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין נִפְרָעִין מִנִּכְסֵי יְתוֹמִין אֶלָּא מִן הַזִּיבּוּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit, lowering the grade of land when collecting from heirs who are יתומים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment from יתומים is collected only from זיבורית.

steps.title: Three payments that cannot be taken from sold land
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that payment for eaten produce, for improvements to land, and for the support of a wife and daughters is not collected from נכסים משועבדים (land the debtor already sold). The reason is תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not collect payment for produce that was eaten, for improvement of land, or for the support of the wife and daughters from property that was sold to others. This is for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list. It names three kinds of payment that can only be collected from land the debtor still owns, not from land he already sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a creditor can take land the debtor sold after the loan, because that land was liened to the debt. These three payments are different. Their amounts are not fixed or not known when the sale happens, so a buyer could never protect himself. To keep buyers from being hurt, the חכמים blocked collection from sold land, and the משנה labels this מפני תיקון העולם.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce that was eaten. Payment owed for fruit a buyer ate from a field that turned out not to belong to the seller.
The increase in value of land, such as improvements the buyer made.
Support for a man's widow and daughters, promised in the כתובה.
Liened property: land the debtor has already sold to someone else.
For the betterment of the world. A rabbinic enactment made to keep society working fairly.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean these payments are not owed at all. They are owed, but they can only be collected from land the debtor still holds or left to his heirs, not from buyers.

phrases.english: We do not collect payment for produce that was eaten,
phrases.notes: Picture a buyer who loses the field and its fruit to the real owner. He can claim the fruit's value from the seller, just not from land the seller sold.

phrases.english: or for the improvement of land,
or for the support of the wife and the daughters
from liened property that was sold to others,
for the betterment of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about which property may be collected from, now naming payments that may never be taken from sold land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment for eaten produce, land improvement, and support of wife and daughters cannot be collected from sold (liened) property, because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: A finder who returns a lost item does not swear
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one who returns a מציאה is not made to take an oath that he kept nothing back, because of תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who finds a lost item does not have to swear, for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more enactment. Someone who returns a lost object is not forced to swear that he returned all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every finder had to swear, people would refuse to return lost items so they would not have to take an oath. Freeing the finder from the oath encourages people to return what they find. That is why this also counts as תיקון העולם.

keyTerms.meaning: One who finds a lost object.
He does not take an oath.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with a list of rabbinic enactments, all labeled מפני תיקון העולם: no collecting from sold land for produce, improvements, or support, and no oath for a finder.

phrases.english: And one who finds a lost item
does not take an oath,
for the betterment of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final, separate enactment to the משנה's list of תיקון העולם rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder who returns a lost item is exempt from an oath, because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: Isn't paying damages from the best land already a Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the label מפני תיקון העולם seems to cover the first rule too, that נזיקין are paid from the best land. But that rule comes straight from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: For the betterment of the world?! It is Torah law, as it is written: 'Of the best of his field and of the best of his vineyard shall he pay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the משנה's reason. It asks how collecting damages from the best land can be called a rabbinic fix when the Torah itself says so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מפני תיקון העולם sounds like it explains every rule in the משנה, including the very first one: נזיקין are paid from עידית. A rabbinic enactment is only needed when the Torah does not already require something. Since the פסוק says 'from the best of his field,' the label looks wrong, and this sets up the answer the גמרא will give next.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah. A Torah law, as opposed to a rabbinic one.
As it is written. Introduces a פסוק.
The best part.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the גמרא treats 'Torah law' and 'rabbinic enactment' as different sources, and a rule cannot simply be given both labels. The answer will have to show what the rabbis actually added.

phrases.english: Gemara: For the betterment of the world?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is aiming at the משנה's first rule, that damages are paid from the best land.

phrases.english: It is Torah law,
as it is written:
'Of the best of his field and of the best of his vineyard shall he pay'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins and challenges how the משנה's closing reason applies to its opening rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim, implied by its closing reason, that collecting נזיקין from עידית is a rabbinic enactment for תיקון העולם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule written explicitly in the Torah does not need a rabbinic reason. The פסוק 'מיטב שדהו' already requires payment from the best land.

steps.title: אביי: The label fits according to רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the question from Step 11. According to רבי ישמעאל, the Torah measures damages by the injured party's best land. Measuring by the damager's land is a rabbinic enactment, made מפני תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The משנה's wording is needed only according to רבי ישמעאל. He holds that by Torah law we measure by the injured party's land. So the משנה is teaching us that because of תיקון העולם, we measure by the damager's land.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from Step 11. He explains why the משנה can call the נזיקין rule 'תיקון העולם' even though it seems to come from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that the פסוק itself says to measure by the damager's best land. אביי says that is only רבי עקיבא's reading. According to רבי ישמעאל, the Torah points to the injured party's land, so switching to the damager's land is a rabbinic fix, and the label fits.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for… (this teaching is needed only for a certain view or case)
We assess / measure (which land is used to measure the payment)
The injured party
The one who caused the damage
By Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as being about the injured party's land, while the rabbinic fix measures by the damager's land.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is needed only according to Rabbi Yishmael,
who says that by Torah law
we assess by the injured party's [land];
it teaches us
that because of the betterment of the world, we assess by the damager's [land].

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to one תנא's view (רבי ישמעאל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Measuring by the damager's best land is plain Torah law, so the label 'תיקון העולם' makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי ישמעאל, Torah law measures by the injured party's land. Measuring by the damager's land is a rabbinic fix.

steps.title: Where is רבי ישמעאל's view found?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where אביי got this view of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this view of רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the רבי ישמעאל view that אביי quoted. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole answer depends on רבי ישמעאל holding that we measure by the injured party's land. Before going further, the גמרא wants to see where he says this.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asking for the source or meaning)

phrases.english: What is [the view of] Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view used in Step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי ישמעאל rules that damages are measured by the injured party's land

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue over 'מיטב'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings the argument. רבי ישמעאל reads 'מיטב שדהו' as the injured party's best land. רבי עקיבא says the פסוק lets injured parties collect from the damager's best land (עידית), and by a קל וחומר so does הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: 'The best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay.' This means the best of the injured party's field and the best of the injured party's vineyard. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: The פסוק comes only to let injured parties collect from the best land, and all the more so הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. It shows רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא reading the same פסוק in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the word 'his' in 'his field' means the injured party's field, so payment is measured by the injured party's best land. For רבי עקיבא, 'his' means the damager's field, so the injured party collects from the damager's עידית. A קל וחומר then teaches that הקדש collects from עידית too.

keyTerms.meaning: The best (quality)
The best-quality land
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one ('all the more so')
Property belonging to the Temple treasury
As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument is the basis for אביי's answer. Only according to רבי ישמעאל is measuring by the damager's land a rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: As it is taught [in a baraita]:
"Of the best of his field and of the best of his vineyard shall he pay"
the best of the field of the injured party,
and the best of the vineyard of the injured party;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
The verse comes only
to let injured parties collect from the best land,
and all the more so for the Temple treasury.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא מֵיטַב שָׂדֵהוּ וּמֵיטַב כַּרְמוֹ יְשַׁלֵּם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל reads 'מיטב' as the injured party's best land, against רבי עקיבא who reads it as the damager's עידית.

steps.title: Why pay for good land if the animal ate poor land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. If the animal ate a poor-quality bed, how can the owner be made to pay for a good-quality one?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי ישמעאל: if the animal ate a rich bed, he pays for a rich one. But if it ate a poor bed, does he pay for a rich one?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי ישמעאל's reading as unfair. If we always measure by the injured party's best land, the damager would overpay when only poor land was damaged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying for good land when good land was eaten makes sense. But measuring every payment by the injured party's best land means paying for good land even when poor land was eaten. That is more than the actual loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Rich (good-quality) garden bed
Poor (low-quality) garden bed

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yishmael,
if [the animal] ate a rich [bed], he pays for a rich one;
if it ate a poor one, does he pay for a rich one?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָכַל שְׁמֵנָה מְשַׁלֵּם שְׁמֵנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of רבי ישמעאל quoted in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's reading that payment is measured by the injured party's best land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would force the damager to pay more than the real loss when the animal ate poor land.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין: When we don't know which bed was eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין limits רבי ישמעאל's rule. It applies only when the animal ate one bed among many and we don't know whether it was rich or poor. In that case he pays from the best.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: Here we are dealing with a case where the animal ate one bed among other beds. We don't know whether it ate a poor one or a rich one, so he pays from the best.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין defends רבי ישמעאל. He limits the rule to a case where we don't know which kind of bed was eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל does not mean a damager pays for good land when we know poor land was eaten. He only means that when it is unclear which bed was eaten, payment is set by the best.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrowed case)
Garden bed

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where [the animal] ate a garden bed among the garden beds,
and we do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּחוּשָׁה אָכַל אִי שְׁמֵנָה אָכַל,
phrases.english: whether it ate a poor one or ate a rich one,
that he pays him from the best.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל makes the damager pay for good land even when we know poor land was eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only when we don't know which bed was eaten.

steps.title: רבא: The one who claims money must bring proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב אידי בר אבין's answer. If knowing it was poor means paying for poor, not knowing should not mean paying for rich, because the one who takes money from another must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If we knew it ate a poor bed, he would pay for a poor one. Now that we don't know, should he pay for a rich one?! Whoever takes money from his fellow must bring the proof!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב אידי בר אבין's answer using a basic rule of money cases: the one making the claim has to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being unsure should not make the damager pay more than he would if we knew the facts. Under המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה, the injured party cannot collect for a rich bed unless he proves a rich bed was eaten. So the narrowed case does not save רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who wants to take money from another must bring proof
If we would know

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with רבי ישמעאל himself. He is rejecting רב אידי בר אבין's way of explaining רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If we knew that it ate a poor one,
he would pay for a poor one;
now that we do not know,
does he pay for a rich one?!
The one who takes [money] from his fellow, the burden of proof is on him!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב אידי בר אבין's narrowed case of not knowing which bed was eaten
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doubt cannot cost the damager more than certainty would, because the claimant carries the burden of proof.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב begins a new answer
steps.stepSummary: Since רבא rejected the first answer, the גמרא turns to a new explanation from רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא drops רב אידי בר אבין's answer and introduces רב אחא בר יעקב, whose explanation comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows that the earlier answer has been dropped. A new way to explain רבי ישמעאל's view is about to be given.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous answer and starts a new one)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's rejection in Step 17, opens a new answer to the קשיא of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation (introduced here, given in the following text)
